claims.explanation: MG-132 is a proteasome inhibitor, and its selectivity likely reflects dependence on proteasome-mediated degradation of pro-apoptotic or stress-response proteins, with TP53 pathway status and NF-kB/ubiquitin-proteasome network activity as key determinants. Lines with TP53 mutations or impaired p53 signaling may be less able to mount a protective response, while high NF-kB activity or specific E3 ligase/ubiquitin pathway alterations could sensitize cells to proteasome inhibition. The virtual cell data showing upregulation of BAG3, CDKN1A, and PMAIP1 (NOXA) supports a stress/apoptotic response mechanism.

features.basis: Most selectively killed lines harbor TP53 mutations, while several least affected lines also have TP53 mutations, suggesting context-dependent but overall association with sensitivity.
NF-kB is constitutively active in AML stem cells and proteasome inhibition blocks NF-kB, potentially sensitizing NF-kB-dependent tumors.
Virtual cell shows RELB upregulation, indicating NF-kB pathway engagement and potential dependence on proteasome for NF-kB activation.
BAG3 is upregulated in virtual cell response; BAG3 is a co-chaperone involved in protein quality control and apoptosis, and its induction may reflect proteotoxic stress.
CDKN1A (p21) upregulation in virtual cell suggests p53 pathway activation and cell cycle arrest, which may contribute to sensitivity.
PMAIP1 (NOXA) upregulation in virtual cell indicates pro-apoptotic BH3-only protein induction, promoting apoptosis under proteasome inhibition.
FBXW7 mutations appear in several selectively killed lines (NCIH1648, SNUC5, MKN1), potentially disrupting ubiquitin-mediated degradation of oncoproteins.
PTEN mutations are present in several sensitive lines (786O, UACC62, FTC133), possibly linking PI3K/AKT activation to proteasome dependence.
PIK3CA mutations appear in multiple sensitive lines (SNU840, HGC27, SNUC5, MKN1), suggesting PI3K pathway activation may increase proteasome dependence.
NF2 mutations in sensitive lines (SNU840, SNU410, S117) may alter Hippo signaling and proteostasis.
ATM mutations in sensitive lines (786O, SNUC5, SNU685) could impair DNA damage response, enhancing sensitivity to proteasome inhibition.
KMT2D mutations appear in both sensitive and resistant lines, but enrichment in some resistant lines (HEC265, BICR6) suggests possible protective role.
